# Copilot instructions for Loki

## Build, test, and lint

Run commands from the repository root with the checked-in Gradle wrapper:

```bash
./gradlew assembleDebug
./gradlew test
./gradlew lintDebug
```

The app targets Android API 35, supports API 29+, uses Java/Kotlin 17, and currently builds native libraries for `arm64-v8a` only. Native builds are configured as Release builds with `-O3`, `-DNDEBUG`, and ARMv8.2 dot-product/FP16 flags; keep those settings aligned in the LLM and STT CMake/Gradle configuration.

Run one unit-test class or method with Gradle's `--tests` filter. Module task paths use the included-project names:

```bash
./gradlew :core:conversation:testDebugUnitTest \
  --tests dev.loki.android.core.conversation.ConversationManagerTest
./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest \
  --tests dev.loki.android.llm.GrammarBuilderTest.testGrammarBuilderFromRegistry
```

On a connected device or emulator, install the debug app with `./gradlew installDebug`. Instrumentation test tasks are available as `:module:connectedDebugAndroidTest` when device tests exist. `docs/SPIKE_1_VALIDATION.md` documents validating the default-assistant and lock-screen flow with `adb`.

## Architecture

Loki is an offline-first Android voice assistant split into an application module and reusable Android library modules declared in `settings.gradle.kts`:

- `app` owns the Android application, Hilt setup, permissions/first-run navigation, and `MainActivity`.
- `core:assistant` integrates with Android's `VoiceInteractionService`, creates voice-interaction sessions, renders the assistant overlay, and maps lifecycle events into `AssistantSession`.
- `core:conversation` owns `ConversationManager`/`ConversationSession`, conversation context, turn logging, JSON tool-call parsing, and the ReAct-style loop. Chat uses a persistent context (up to 10 turns); each voice invocation gets an ephemeral one-turn context.
- `core:tools` defines tool contracts, permission-aware registration/dispatch, and result/error types. `core:tools:local` supplies the built-in on-device tools. Register new tools in `DefaultLocalTools.registerAll`.
- `core:llm` exposes `LlmEngine` and model discovery. `LlamaCppLlmEngine` loads GGUF models through `core/llm/src/main/cpp/loki_llama_bridge.cpp`; `LiteRtLlmEngine` loads LiteRT `.bin` models through MediaPipe. `AppModule` selects LiteRT only when a LiteRT model exists without a GGUF model; otherwise it selects llama.cpp.
- `core:voice:stt` records 16 kHz microphone audio and transcribes it with Whisper through `loki_whisper_bridge.cpp`. `core:voice:tts` wraps Android's local `TextToSpeech`.
- `core:ui` contains Compose screens, view models, theme persistence, setup/permission UI, and the chat/session overlay.

The normal voice path is Android assistant invocation -> `LokiVoiceInteractionSession` -> `AssistantSession` -> `SttEngine` -> `ConversationSession` -> grammar-constrained LLM JSON -> `ToolRegistry` -> optional fast-path response -> TTS. The text path uses `ChatViewModel` and the same conversation/tool pipeline with TTS disabled.

The two upstream native engines are Git submodules at `core/llm/src/main/cpp/llama.cpp` and `core/voice/stt/src/main/cpp/whisper.cpp`. Treat their source and their local `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md` as upstream-owned; Loki-specific integration belongs in the surrounding CMake files, JNI bridges, and Kotlin wrappers.

## Repository-specific conventions

- Use Kotlin official style and the existing module dependency direction. Put cross-cutting dependencies behind interfaces (`LlmEngine`, `SttEngine`, `TtsEngine`, `Tool`) and wire production implementations as Hilt singletons in `app/src/main/java/dev/loki/android/di/AppModule.kt`.
- Keep inference and audio work off the main thread using coroutines/Flows. Expose lifecycle/progress through sealed state or event types and preserve cancellation: assistant/session teardown calls STT, LLM, and TTS cancellation/stop methods.
- Tool metadata is part of prompting and grammar generation. A tool must provide a stable `name`, description, parameter definitions, and required Android permissions; permission checks happen both when constructing the available/disabled tool prompt and before execution.
- LLM responses are constrained to the JSON shape generated by `GrammarBuilder` and parsed by `ToolCallParser`. Preserve the distinction between `{"tool": ..., "arguments": ...}` and `{"response": ...}` rather than adding ad-hoc natural-language parsing.
- Model files are discovered from the app external files directory first, then internal files, using `model.gguf`/`model.bin` defaults or the first matching extension. Do not check in model binaries; build outputs, APKs/AARs, `.cxx`, and local Gradle state are ignored.
- Native code is intentionally a narrow bridge: keep JNI handle ownership, cancellation, model release, and logging consistent with the existing bridge implementations. Do not edit vendored engine internals for Loki behavior.
- Compose UI state is collected from `StateFlow`; persistent theme mode and first-run completion belong in `ThemeRepository`/DataStore rather than activity-only state.
- For work tracked through the repository's OpenSpec workflow, use `openspec/config.yaml` and keep proposals, specs, designs, and tasks under `openspec/changes/`. Read the relevant change artifacts before implementing or changing behavior.
- The feasibility and device-validation notes in `docs/SPIKE_1_VALIDATION.md`, `docs/SPIKE_2_VALIDATION.md`, and `docs/SPIKE_3_VALIDATION.md` are the source of truth for assistant invocation, native tool calling, and end-to-end offline voice behavior.
